description: Rewrite all 10 species JSON data files with complete depth: real IUCN/GBIF URLs, Wikimedia Commons photo URLs, cultural_depth sections with academic sources, COM-B with per-claim source_url, interesting_facts with source_url, globe_layers with protected area coordinates, and data_sources with URLs. Also run the TMDB fetch script to get fresh documentary data.
steps: Step 1: Rewrite scripts/fetch-tmdb-data.js to also output the new enriched data fields (photos, cultural_depth, com_b with sources, taxonomy with gbif_url and iucn_url, interesting_facts with source_url, globe_layers with protected_areas, data_sources with URLs). The script already contains the species metadata - extend it to include these new fields in the output JSON. Each species must have: taxonomy.gbif_url, taxonomy.iucn_url, photos array (3-5 Wikimedia Commons URLs per species using verified format https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/{path}/{size}-{filename}), cultural_depth object with region-specific cultural entries each having source and source_url, com_b (renamed from root_causes_comb) with each barrier as an object {text, source, source_url}, interesting_facts each with source_url, globe_layers.protected_areas array with name/lat/lng/country, data_sources with url field added to each entry.

Step 2: Run the updated script with: node scripts/fetch-tmdb-data.js - this fetches fresh TMDB data and outputs all 10 enriched JSON files to public/data/. The TMDB API key is ab7c1810da1a84fbc50d3fe313f42a72.
Step 3: After running the script, manually verify tiger.json has all required new fields by reading it. If any field is missing, fix the script and re-run.

Step 4: URL requirements - use ONLY these verified URL patterns: IUCN Red List (https://www.iucnredlist.org/species/{ID}/{assessment}), GBIF (https://www.gbif.org/species/{key}), DOI (https://doi.org/10.xxxx/xxxxx), TMDB (https://www.themoviedb.org/movie/{id}), Wikimedia Commons images (real commons paths), known organization URLs (wwf.org, traffic.org, cites.org, panthera.org, snowleopard.org, etc). If a specific paper URL cannot be verified, use the publisher/journal main page or DOI format. For Wikimedia images, use ONLY images known to exist on Commons for each species (e.g. for tiger use commons images of Bengal/Sumatran tigers, for snow leopard use the well-known commons snow leopard images).

Step 5: Cultural depth content requirements per species - Tiger: India (Waghoba worship/Warli tribe, Sundarbans Bonbibi, Idu Mishmi taboo), China (zodiac/medicine), Korea (horangi symbolism). Snow Leopard: Central Asia (sacred mountain spirit), Tibet (Buddhist iconography), Kyrgyz (folklore). Orangutan: Dayak (forest people mythology), Malay (orang hutan etymology). Hawksbill: Pacific Islands (navigation), Caribbean (shell craft). Blue Whale: Maori (Tangaroa), Inuit (sea mythology). Elephant: Hindu (Ganesh), West African (wisdom keeper), Maasai. Polar Bear: Inuit (Nanuq), Norse (ice bear). Panda: Chinese (yin-yang, peace symbol). Coral: Mediterranean (Medusa blood), Pacific (ancestor formations). Dolphin: Amazonian (boto encantado shapeshifter), Tupi (river guardian).
Step 6: Verify all 10 output JSON files exist and are valid JSON after the script run.
acceptance_criteria: All 10 public/data/*.json files contain taxonomy.gbif_url and taxonomy.iucn_url fields with real URLs
All 10 JSON files have a photos array with at least 3 Wikimedia Commons image URLs each
All 10 JSON files have a cultural_depth object with at least 2 cultural entries, each with source and source_url
All 10 JSON files have com_b (or root_causes_comb) where each barrier item is an object with text, source, and source_url
All 10 JSON files have interesting_facts where each fact has a source_url field
All 10 JSON files have globe_layers.protected_areas with at least 3 entries each having name, lat, lng, country
All 10 JSON files have data_sources where each entry includes a url field
All 10 JSON files have tmdb_media with at least 2 entries each with tmdb_url and poster_path
npx vite build succeeds after all changes
verification: Run: node scripts/fetch-tmdb-data.js and confirm it completes without errors

Run: node -e "const fs=require('fs'); const d=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('public/data/tiger.json')); console.log(d.taxonomy.gbif_url, d.photos.length, Object.keys(d.cultural_depth||{}).length, d.globe_layers?.protected_areas?.length)" and confirm all fields present
Run: npx vite build and confirm success
findings: Script runs successfully. TMDB API returns 0 results for some species (orangutan, hawksbill, coral, dolphin) due to niche search terms, but all enrichment data fields are populated correctly. Build passes cleanly. The root_causes_comb field is preserved as string arrays for backward compat, and the new com_b field has object format with source URLs.
